description: Hello! We're from different backgrounds that have interest in health, science, and space. We want to help solve real-life problems to put into good use. Join us on this journey to explore about the human life in space into helping them keep in track of their health as they maintain in discovering, learning, and informing us about space. A young enthusiast innovator and mind creates a better future.
summary: We developed ASTRA, a mission-focused crew health decision-support prototype designed to help astronauts and medical teams track long-term spaceflight risks in one unified view. Because microgravity-induced bone and muscle loss and deep-space ionizing radiation affect the body quietly and continuously, scattered readings make early warning signs easy to miss. ASTRA addresses this gap through a clear Collect, Interpret, and Respond workflow—gathering physiological measurements, radiation readings, and daily checklists, checking them against defined thresholds, and classifying status into Normal, Warning, or Critical levels. Built as a practical decision-support tool rather than a replacement for professional medical judgment, ASTRA turns complex biomedical telemetry into accessible, actionable health signals so crews can spot developing trends early and respond effectively during long-duration missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

ASTRA is a mission-focused crew health decision-support prototype designed to consolidate fragmented physiological and environmental telemetry into one clear, actionable dashboard. During long-duration spaceflight, subtle health changes accumulate quietly and continuously—making developing risks easy to miss if data is scattered.


ASTRA focuses on two primary spaceflight hazards:

Bone & Muscle Changes (Physical Health): Monitors microgravity-induced bone density loss, muscle deconditioning, and daily crew exercise/health checklists.
Space Radiation (Environmental Risk): Tracks ionizing radiation exposure beyond typical Earth conditions so cumulative risks are continuously understood.
The system operates through a structured three-step workflow:

Key Benefits & Intended Impact Early Signal Detection:

Bridges the gap between scattered raw telemetry and early intervention by bringing bone, muscle, and radiation indicators together in one unified view.


Reduced Alert Fatigue: Separates routine daily tracking from genuine anomalies using a clean three-tier status framework, ensuring not every minor fluctuation is treated as an emergency.
Human-Centered Decision Support: Turns complex physiological and radiation readings into accessible, actionable guidance that supports both astronauts onboard and medical teams reviewing mission trends.

Collect: Gathers physiological measurements, radiation readings, and daily crew checklists in one place.

Interpret: Applies rules-based health logic to evaluate incoming values against defined thresholds and flag unusual trends early.

Respond: Translates those signals into a clear three-level status system—Normal (within defined limits, routine tracking continues), Warning (unusual change requiring trend review and follow-up), and Critical (high-priority trigger requiring prompt review by medical professionals)

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

1. Frontend Development & Interactivity: React.js and TypeScript were used to build the interactive single-page web application, with Tailwind CSS for responsive styling and UI design. Vite was used as the frontend development and build tool. The interface includes dynamic dashboards, health indicators, interactive components, mission telemetry visualization and real-time UI state updates using simulated mission data.

2. Backend Development & Database Management: Python and FastAPI were used to develop the backend REST API, handling health measurements, radiation readings, alerts, recommendations and daily checklists. SQLAlchemy was used for database operations, with SQLite for structured data storage. Uvicorn was used to run the backend server.

3. Reporting & Documentation: ReportLab was used to generate downloadable PDF health reports containing astronaut health measurements, radiation records and alerts.

4. Research & Data Synthesis: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) resources and spaceflight health research informed the project's bone and muscle health monitoring, radiation-risk indicators and preventive-care recommendations. The current prototype uses simulated mission data to demonstrate these functionalities.

Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered Creativity:

Rather than overwhelming users with raw scientific graphs or overpromising autonomous medical diagnosis, ASTRA focuses on signal clarity. By pairing a simple Collect → Interpret → Respond pipeline with intuitive color-coded triage cards, it bridges the gap between complex biomedical data and rapid human comprehension.

Factors Considered:

1. Clinical Realism & Safety: Explicitly scoped ASTRA as a practical decision-support tool—not a replacement for professional medical judgment—ensuring Critical alerts prompt proper medical review.

2. Cognitive Load & Visual Hierarchy: Designed a high-contrast dark-space UI with clear visual separation between physical health (Bone & Muscle) and environmental risk (Space Radiation) so signals are easy to scan at a glance.

3. Actionability Over Noise: Built around threshold-based rules so crew members know immediately whether to continue routine monitoring, review a developing trend, or escalate an urgent condition.
